# The Weaver of Dawn

In the time before time, darkness covered all the world. The people huddled in caves, cold and afraid, knowing nothing of light or warmth.

High in the mountains lived an old woman named Ayana, who spent her days weaving at her loom. Her fingers worked ceaselessly, though she could not see the threads she wove in the endless night.

One evening, Ayana's granddaughter asked, "Grandmother, what are you making in this darkness?"

"I am weaving the dawn," Ayana replied. "Each thread is a prayer, each pattern a promise. When my tapestry is complete, light will come to the world."

The granddaughter laughed. "But you cannot even see your work!"

"That is precisely why I must weave," Ayana said. "Faith requires no eyes."

For seven years, Ayana wove without ceasing. Her fingers bled onto the threads, adding crimson to the tapestry. On the final day, she tied the last knot and held up her work.

The tapestry blazed with colors never seen before—gold, orange, pink, and red. It rose from her hands into the sky, unfurling across the horizon. And thus the first sunrise was born, woven from an old woman's faith and sacrifice.

Now, each dawn remembers Ayana's gift to the world.
